clue.text: Spiteful about husband and inclined to gossip

indicators.note: about means going round, so the spiteful word is wrapped around the husband's letter

parts.note: spiteful means catty

explanation.surface: Someone malicious about a husband and fond of gossiping.
explanation.definitionFit: A talkative person who loves a natter is described with this adjective, a near synonym of gossipy.

clue.text: Opposing lines revealed in talk

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
verse is lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Contrary lines of argument emerge in a discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposing' looks like the definition (the adjective meaning opposite) but supplies CON; the definition is 'talk'.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat or hold a conversation is a synonym of talk as a verb.

clue.text: A trick when recipe's included fruit we can't eat

indicators.note: included means the recipe letter is taken inside the word for a trick

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, seen on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A kitchen trick where the recipe includes an inedible fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' puts R inside CON, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: The oak's nut is the tree's fruit, though not one people eat.

clue.text: Mum put in item of furniture that may get broken

indicators.note: put in means the word for mum is placed inside the furniture

parts.note: a table is a piece of furniture
Ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Mother placed in a piece of furniture likely to get broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' is meant as broken in, like a horse: domesticated.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild horse is broken in, so one that can be trained is capable of domestication.

clue.text: Symbol of victory Parliament put back in old city

indicators.note: in places the turned Parliament letters inside the name of the ancient city

parts.note: Troy is the ancient city of Homer's Iliad

indicators.note: put back tells us to read the Parliament abbreviation backwards

parts.note: HP stands for the Houses of Parliament

explanation.surface: A token of triumph returned by Parliament to an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses the Parliament abbreviation and 'in' nests it in the city; Troy is the city besieged by the Greeks.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup or statuette awarded to a winner is the classic emblem of success.

clue.text: You can't trust an agent to be honest giving answers

definitions.text: You can't trust an agent to be honest

explanation.surface: Agents are not reliable when they respond.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition splits the answer into REP (agent) and LIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Responses to questions are a synonym, and split up the word says a representative is untruthful.

clue.text: Artist making plea getting awful rot accepted

indicators.note: accepted means the jumbled letters are taken inside the plea

parts.note: a prayer is a plea

indicators.note: awful suggests something messed up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter begs after being given dreadful rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist' here is anyone who depicts, so an actor portraying a role counts; 'awful' scrambles the rot and 'accepted' takes it in.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who depicts others, as a painter or actor does, is a depicter or portraitist.

clue.text: American jerk starts to enrage Englishmen

parts.note: to yank is to jerk

indicators.note: starts to means taking the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A US idiot begins to annoy the English.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial term for a person from the United States.

clue.text: Consistently successful journalist is well-educated

parts.note: a team that keeps winning is in form
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter who keeps doing well is also learned.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone knowledgeable and well-read is described as having plenty of knowledge, a near synonym.

clue.text: Puts off performance in East Anglian town

indicators.note: in means the performance sits inside the town's name

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, in eastern England
a concert is a musical performance

explanation.surface: Some show in a Norfolk town is postponed.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle or fluster someone is to throw them off balance.

clue.text: Maybe mother or father given periodic payment

parts.note: p.a., per annum, describes something recurring every year
rent is a regular payment for accommodation

explanation.surface: A mum or dad receiving a regular allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: PA here is per annum (yearly), not the father it seems to suggest; the definition is a parent by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother and father are each examples of the general word for someone who has a child.

clue.text: Eager to express grief

definitions.meaning: an eager person is enthusiastic, sharp and ready
to wail in mourning over the dead, as at an Irish wake

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means enthusiastic, and the verb means to lament loudly for someone who has died.

clue.text: Animal books better than all others one's given stars

parts.note: the best is superior to all the rest
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's means 'has'
Aries is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: Superior wildlife volumes rated with stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval collections of descriptions of real and imaginary creatures were known by this name.

clue.text: Something sung in film when the enemy walks past?

definitions.meaning: the famous song played by Sam in the film Casablanca
time is the proverbial enemy, so this is a whimsical description of the hours passing

explanation.definitionFit: The title of the Casablanca song also literally describes time moving on, here dubbed the enemy.

clue.text: Start eating, sit around in proper positions

indicators.note: the letters are moved around and set in their proper places, an anagram signal

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tuck in, and gather round in your correct seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' looks like part of the meal instructions but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something in motion or initiate it, a synonym of begin.

clue.text: Illustration in a new church includes saint

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A picture in a newly built church shows a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' slips the saint in straight after the first word, so the church letters CE end the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An example cited to show something, as in 'for example', is an illustration.

clue.text: Sterling Cafe badly organised with DIY facility?

indicators.note: something badly organised has its parts muddled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A café run chaotically, where you have to make your own food.
explanation.definitionFit: Holiday accommodation where guests cook their own meals is described as do-it-yourself in its catering arrangements.

clue.text: Article stuck in bank of river down below

indicators.note: stuck in means the article is wedged inside the word for bank

parts.note: to bank is to tilt or lean, as an aircraft does
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: An item lodged in the bank of a river downstream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is the verb, tilt; 'down below' is the underworld, where Lethe flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethe is the river of forgetfulness in the Greek underworld, so this adjective relates to it.

clue.text: One could make leap to edge of pond — after transformation!

definitions.text: One could make leap to edge of pond — after transformation!

indicators.note: transformation changes the form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: edge of takes the letter at the edge of pond, its last

explanation.surface: A creature that leaps to the pond's edge once it has changed form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after transformation' rearranges LEAPTO with D, the last letter of pond.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog larva, once metamorphosed, becomes a frog that could jump to the pond's edge.

clue.text: Very light one of them may be

definitions.text: Very light one of them may be

parts.words: Very light one of them may be
parts.note: a Very light is a signal fired from a pistol, and so belongs to that class of signals

explanation.walkthrough: 'Very light' seems to mean extremely light, but it is the Very pistol signal, named after its inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright signal flashes fired to attract attention include the Very light.

clue.text: Secluded Conservative girl meets the heartless revolutionary

parts.note: Lois is a girl's name

indicators.note: heartless means losing the middle letter, so the outer pair remains

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A reclusive Tory woman encounters an ailing revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle out of THE, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloister is a monastic enclosure, so a sheltered, withdrawn life is described this way.

clue.text: Place that makes sense by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for a sense is heard, not spelt

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: A location that seems sensible when you hear about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A location or plot where something stands or is to be built is a synonym.

clue.text: Outburst of colossal volume

indicators.note: of signals the answer is made from part of these words

explanation.surface: A huge volume of noise erupting.
explanation.definitionFit: A burst of gunfire or of words, a simultaneous discharge, is an outburst.

clue.text: Hidden stem by a river

parts.note: a cane is a plant stem, as in sugar cane

explanation.surface: A concealed plant stalk next to a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge understood only by a few is secret, obscure and so hidden.

clue.text: Country wants tax to come down

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free
to land is to come down to earth

explanation.surface: A nation demands that taxes be cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern part of the United Kingdom is a country in its own right.

clue.text: Back English author

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Support for an English writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was the eighteenth-century novelist behind Tristram Shandy.

clue.text: Go away and ask somebody

parts.note: to beg is to ask earnestly
one means a person, somebody

explanation.surface: Telling someone to leave and then asking someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned imperative ordering someone to leave, like 'be off'.
